topics.label: Lecture introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, contextualises the difficulty of complement nomenclature, and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Foundational principles, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic architecture, naming conventions, and central molecular hub of the complement system.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical routes that trigger complement activation and converge on C3 convertase formation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream mechanisms by which activated complement clears pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and inhibitors that protect host cells from complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how deficiencies in specific complement components manifest in distinct clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies that pathogens employ to survive complement-mediated immune clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the adaptive immune system
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming topic on adaptive immunity.
